q: 'CONCERT', developed by the Centre for Railway Information Systems (CRIS), is the software platform which powers:
e: CONCERT is the software developed by CRIS that powers the Passenger Reservation System (PRS), handling computerised reservation of berths and seats across India.

q: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh (RRSK), a fund created in 2017-18 for financing safety-related works of Indian Railways, had a corpus of:
e: The Rashtriya Rail Sanraksha Kosh was created in the Budget 2017-18 with a corpus of Rs 1 lakh crore, built up over five years to finance safety-related works of Indian Railways.

q: The Bombay-Thane railway line of 1853, the first in India, was also the first railway line to be opened in:
e: The Bombay-Thane line of 1853 was not only the first railway line in India but also the first railway line to be opened anywhere in Asia.

q: The first train in northern India was run in 1859 between:
e: The first train in northern India ran in 1859 between Allahabad and Kanpur, a few years after the Bombay-Thane and Howrah-Hooghly lines.

q: The highest railway station in the world, Tanggula, situated at an altitude of over 5,000 metres, is located in:
e: Tanggula station in China, on the Qinghai-Tibet railway at an altitude of over 5,000 metres, is the highest railway station in the world.

q: Originally, the Constitution of India contained how many Articles?
e: The Constitution of India as originally adopted contained 395 Articles, though amendments have since taken the total well beyond that figure.

q: Originally, the Constitution of India had how many Schedules?
e: The Constitution originally had 8 Schedules; four more were added by amendments, taking the total to 12.

q: The first general elections in independent India were held in:
e: The first general elections in independent India were held in 1951-52, after the Constitution came into force in January 1950.

q: Who was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India?
e: Justice M. Fathima Beevi, appointed in 1989, was the first woman judge of the Supreme Court of India.

q: The Constitution of India has been described as 'quasi-federal' by:
e: K.C. Wheare described the Indian Constitution as quasi-federal, meaning federal in form but unitary in spirit and features.

q: Article 23 of the Constitution of India prohibits:

options.B: Traffic in human beings and forced labour

e: Article 23 prohibits traffic in human beings and forced labour (begar); untouchability is covered by Article 17 and abolition of titles by Article 18.

q: Telangana became a separate State, carved out of Andhra Pradesh, in the year:
e: Telangana became a separate State on 2 June 2014, carved out of Andhra Pradesh under the Andhra Pradesh Reorganisation Act.

q: The Ashok Mehta Committee (1977) was appointed to review the working of:
e: The Ashok Mehta Committee of 1977 was appointed to review the working of Panchayati Raj institutions and recommended a two-tier structure.

q: Annie Besant launched the Home Rule League in 1916 at:
e: Annie Besant launched her Home Rule League in 1916 at Adyar in Madras; Tilak had launched his league earlier the same year at Poona.

q: During the Revolt of 1857, the resistance at Jhansi was led by:
e: During the Revolt of 1857, the resistance at Jhansi was led by Rani Lakshmibai, who died fighting the British near Gwalior.

q: The Vernacular Press Act, 1878 was enacted during the viceroyalty of:
e: The Vernacular Press Act of 1878 was enacted during the viceroyalty of Lord Lytton to control Indian-language newspapers; it was repealed by Lord Ripon.

q: The 'Rajatarangini', a chronicle of the kings of Kashmir, was written by:
e: The Rajatarangini, a Sanskrit chronicle of the kings of Kashmir, was written by the Kashmiri historian Kalhana in the 12th century.

q: The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of:
e: The Chinese pilgrim Fa-Hien visited India during the reign of the Gupta emperor Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya) in the early 5th century.

q: The 'Ashtapradhan' was the council of eight ministers of:
e: The Ashtapradhan was the council of eight ministers of Chhatrapati Shivaji, with the Peshwa as its head.

q: The Ajanta Caves, famous for their ancient murals, are located in the State of:
e: The Ajanta Caves, famous for their ancient Buddhist murals and sculptures, are located in Maharashtra near Aurangabad.

q: The Khalsa Panth was founded by Guru Gobind Singh in the year:
e: Guru Gobind Singh, the tenth Sikh Guru, founded the Khalsa Panth in 1699 at Anandpur Sahib on the occasion of Baisakhi.

q: The largest lake in the world by surface area is the:
e: The Caspian Sea is the largest lake in the world by surface area, although Lake Baikal holds the largest volume of fresh water.

q: The longest river in the world is the:
e: The Nile, flowing for about 6,650 km through north-eastern Africa, is regarded as the longest river in the world.

q: K2 (Godwin Austen), the second highest peak in the world, is situated in the:
e: K2 or Godwin Austen, at 8,611 metres the second highest peak in the world, is situated in the Karakoram range.

q: Periyar National Park, well known for its elephants, is located in:
e: Periyar National Park, a well-known elephant and tiger reserve around the Periyar lake, is located at Thekkady in Kerala.

q: Keoladeo Ghana National Park at Bharatpur is world-famous for its:
e: Keoladeo Ghana National Park at Bharatpur in Rajasthan is world-famous as a sanctuary for migratory birds that arrive in winter.

q: The Harappan site of Dholavira is located in the present-day State of:
e: Dholavira, one of the largest Harappan cities, famous for its water reservoirs, is located in the Kachchh district of Gujarat.

q: The Sardar Sarovar Dam is built across the river:
e: The Sardar Sarovar Dam, one of the largest dams of India, is built across the Narmada river in Gujarat.

q: The pre-monsoon thunderstorms in West Bengal are locally known as:
e: Kalbaisakhi are the violent pre-monsoon thunderstorms, also called nor'westers, that occur in West Bengal in the summer months.

q: Which State is the largest producer of coffee in India?
e: Karnataka is the largest producer of coffee in India, growing roughly 70 per cent of the country's total coffee output.

q: The NIFTY index of the National Stock Exchange is based on the share prices of how many companies?
e: The NIFTY, the benchmark index of the National Stock Exchange, is based on the share prices of 50 large companies; the Sensex has 30.

q: The 'Rolling Plan' was introduced in India for the period:
e: The Rolling Plan, under which targets were revised every year, was introduced by the Janata government for the period 1978-80.

q: The first estimate of the national income of India was made by:
e: Dadabhai Naoroji made the first estimate of the national income of India, which he presented in his work on poverty in India.

q: The first Industrial Policy Resolution of independent India was announced in the year:
e: The first Industrial Policy Resolution of independent India was announced in 1948, laying down the framework of a mixed economy.

q: The Human Development Index (HDI) is published annually by the:
e: The Human Development Index is published annually by the United Nations Development Programme in its Human Development Report, based on health, education and income.

q: Under the Mahatma Gandhi National Rural Employment Guarantee Act (MGNREGA), a rural household is entitled to wage employment of up to how many days in a financial year?
e: Wage employment entitlement is now up to 125 days per rural household per year. (Source: Viksit Bharat-Guarantee for Rozgar and Ajeevika Mission (Gramin) (VB-G RAM G) Act, 2025, Section 5(1), replacing MGNREGA 2005; PIB Release ID 2207187 dated 21.12.2025; effective 01.07.2026.)

q: The Theory of Relativity was propounded by:
e: The Theory of Relativity, comprising the special theory of 1905 and the general theory of 1915, was propounded by Albert Einstein.

q: The nucleus of the atom was discovered by:
e: Ernest Rutherford discovered the nucleus of the atom in 1911 through his famous gold-foil scattering experiment.

q: Radioactivity was discovered by:
e: Radioactivity was discovered in 1896 by Henri Becquerel while studying the radiation emitted by uranium salts.

q: The Periodic Table of elements was first systematically arranged by:
e: Dmitri Mendeleev first systematically arranged the elements in the Periodic Table in 1869, based on atomic mass and chemical properties.

q: Who among the following is regarded as the 'Father of the Computer'?
e: Charles Babbage is regarded as the Father of the Computer for designing the Analytical Engine, an early programmable mechanical computer.

q: The full form of RADAR is:
e: RADAR stands for Radio Detection and Ranging, a system that locates objects by means of radio waves.

q: Which blood group is known as the 'universal donor' group?
e: The O blood group is called the universal donor group because its red cells carry neither A nor B antigens.

q: Scurvy is caused by the deficiency of:
e: Scurvy, a disease marked by bleeding gums and weakness, is caused by the deficiency of Vitamin C (ascorbic acid).

q: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was established in the year:
e: The Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) was established on 15 August 1969, succeeding the earlier INCOSPAR committee.

q: The book 'Indica', an account of India of the Mauryan age, was written by:
e: The book Indica, describing India of the Mauryan age, was written by Megasthenes, the Greek ambassador at the court of Chandragupta Maurya.

q: The novel 'A Passage to India' was written by:
e: The novel A Passage to India, set in British India and published in 1924, was written by E.M. Forster.

q: The highest peacetime gallantry award of India is the:
e: The Ashoka Chakra is India's highest peacetime gallantry award; the Param Vir Chakra is the highest gallantry award in wartime.

q: The five interlaced rings on the Olympic flag represent:
e: The five interlaced rings on the Olympic flag represent the five inhabited continents of the world taking part in the Games.

q: Hindi Diwas is celebrated every year on:
e: Hindi Diwas is celebrated on 14 September, marking the day in 1949 when Hindi in the Devanagari script was adopted as an official language.

q: The Howrah division of Indian Railways is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Howrah division, one of the oldest divisions of Indian Railways, is a part of the Eastern Railway with headquarters at Kolkata.

q: The Delhi division of Indian Railways belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Delhi division, which handles the busy Delhi area terminals, belongs to the Northern Railway.

q: The Agra division of Indian Railways is administered by which zonal railway?
e: The Agra division, covering Agra and Mathura, is administered by the North Central Railway headquartered at Prayagraj.

q: The Rangiya division of Indian Railways is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Rangiya division in Assam is a part of the Northeast Frontier Railway, whose headquarters is at Maligaon in Guwahati.

q: The Guntur division of Indian Railways belongs to which zonal railway?
e: Guntur division now belongs to the South Coast Railway (HQ Visakhapatnam). (Source: Ministry of Railways Gazette notification dated 04.05.2026 constituting South Coast Railway; operations from 01.06.2026.)

q: The Hubballi division of Indian Railways is administered by which zonal railway?
e: The Hubballi division is administered by the South Western Railway, which itself has its headquarters at Hubballi.

q: The Sambalpur division of Indian Railways is a part of which zonal railway?
e: The Sambalpur division in western Odisha is a part of the East Coast Railway headquartered at Bhubaneswar.

q: The Jabalpur division of Indian Railways belongs to which zonal railway?
e: The Jabalpur division belongs to the West Central Railway, which has its headquarters at Jabalpur itself.

q: The Vaishali Express, a popular superfast train of Bihar, runs between New Delhi and:
e: The Vaishali Express, a popular superfast train from Bihar, runs between New Delhi and Saharsa.

q: The North East Express runs between Anand Vihar Terminal (Delhi) and:
e: The North East Express runs between Anand Vihar Terminal in Delhi and Kamakhya station at Guwahati in Assam.

q: The Prayag Raj Express, a prestigious overnight train, connects New Delhi with:
e: The Prayag Raj Express, a prestigious overnight superfast train, connects New Delhi with Prayagraj in Uttar Pradesh.

q: The historic Lucknow Mail, among the oldest trains on its route, runs between New Delhi and:
e: The historic Lucknow Mail, running since the metre gauge era, connects New Delhi with Lucknow, the capital of Uttar Pradesh.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Sampoorna Kranti Express runs between Rajendra Nagar Terminal (Patna) and New Delhi.
2. The Shiv Ganga Express runs between Varanasi and New Delhi.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Both statements are correct: the Sampoorna Kranti Express runs between Rajendra Nagar Terminal (Patna) and New Delhi, and the Shiv Ganga Express runs between Varanasi and New Delhi.

q: 'Jan Sadharan' Express trains of Indian Railways are:

options.A: Fully unreserved trains run at the lowest fares for the common man
options.B: Air-conditioned trains meant for young passengers
options.C: Special trains run only for senior citizens
options.D: Luxury tourist trains run on heritage routes

e: Jan Sadharan Express trains are fully unreserved trains run at the lowest fares so that the common man can travel cheaply.

q: 'Yuva' Express trains of Indian Railways were introduced primarily to provide:

options.B: Low-cost air-conditioned travel to the youth and the unemployed
options.C: Reserved travel facilities exclusively to women

e: Yuva Express trains were introduced mainly to provide low-cost air-conditioned travel to the youth and the unemployed.

q: 'Intercity' Express trains of Indian Railways are designed mainly to:

options.B: Carry only freight traffic between ports
options.D: Connect two cities with a day journey, enabling a same-day return

e: Intercity Express trains connect two cities by a day journey, so that passengers can go and return on the same day.

q: Which train is often described as the slowest train in India, taking about five hours to cover roughly 46 km at an average speed of around 10 km per hour?

options.C: The Nilgiri Passenger between Mettupalayam and Udagamandalam

e: The Nilgiri Passenger between Mettupalayam and Udagamandalam is among the slowest trains of India, taking about five hours for roughly 46 km on the steep rack section.

q: The 'Fairy Queen' heritage steam train of Indian Railways runs between:
e: The Fairy Queen heritage steam train, hauled by one of the world's oldest working steam locomotives, runs between Delhi and Alwar in Rajasthan.

q: India's first train powered by CNG (compressed natural gas), introduced in 2015 as an environment-friendly service, ran between:
e: India's first CNG-powered train, introduced in 2015 as a green initiative, ran between Rewari and Rohtak in Haryana.

q: In Indian Railways, the computerised 'CMS', used for managing train crew duties and rosters, stands for:
e: In Indian Railways, CMS stands for Crew Management System, the computerised system used for managing crew duties, rosters and rest of loco pilots and guards.

q: In Indian Railways, 'OBHS', the service through which cleaning of coaches and toilets is provided on demand during a journey, stands for:
e: OBHS stands for On-Board Housekeeping Service, under which cleaning of coaches and toilets is provided on demand during a journey.

q: In railway signalling, 'TPWS', a safety system provided on some sections to prevent trains from passing signals at danger, stands for:
e: TPWS stands for Train Protection and Warning System, a safety system that applies brakes if a train passes a signal at danger.

q: In railway engineering, 'USFD', the technique used for detecting internal defects and cracks in rails, stands for:
e: USFD stands for Ultrasonic Flaw Detection, the technique used to detect internal defects, cracks and flaws in rails.

q: The 'RRTS', the high-speed regional commuter rail system being developed in the National Capital Region, stands for:
e: RRTS stands for Regional Rapid Transit System, the high-speed regional commuter rail network being developed in the National Capital Region.

q: In railway reservation, the emergency quota commonly called the 'HO quota' is released under the authority of senior officers, the letters 'HO' standing for:
e: The HO quota is the High Official quota, the emergency quota in train reservation released under the authority of senior officers.

q: In Indian Railways, the abbreviation 'TTE', used for the ticket-checking staff on trains, stands for:
e: TTE stands for Travelling Ticket Examiner, the staff member who checks tickets of passengers on running trains.

q: The Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC), which runs the e-ticketing and catering services of Indian Railways, was incorporated in the year:
e: The Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation (IRCTC) was incorporated in 1999 as a public sector undertaking under the Ministry of Railways.

q: The Railway Claims Tribunal, which settles compensation claims relating to railway accidents and goods, was set up under an Act enacted in the year:
e: The Railway Claims Tribunal was set up under the Railway Claims Tribunal Act of 1987 to settle compensation claims for accidents and goods.

q: The Fog Safety Device (FogPASS) provided in locomotives primarily helps the loco pilot to:

options.A: Increase the speed of the train in fog
options.B: Communicate with the guard of the train
options.C: Know the location and approach of signals in foggy weather
options.D: Detect passengers standing on the track

e: The Fog Safety Device (FogPASS), based on GPS, helps the loco pilot know the location and approach of signals and stations in foggy weather.

q: In modern three-phase electric locomotives of Indian Railways, 'regenerative braking' means that during braking:

options.A: The brakes are applied jointly by the guard and the driver
options.B: The traction motors act as generators and feed electrical energy back to the overhead equipment
options.C: Sand is dropped on the rails to improve adhesion
options.D: The braking energy is stored in batteries fitted under the coaches

e: In regenerative braking, the traction motors work as generators during braking and feed electrical energy back into the overhead equipment, saving power.

q: On electrified sections of Indian Railways, a 'tower wagon' (tower car) is a self-propelled vehicle used for:

options.A: Inspection and maintenance of the overhead electric equipment (OHE)
options.C: Hauling freight wagons within a yard
options.D: Lifting derailed coaches at accident sites

e: A tower wagon or tower car is a self-propelled vehicle used for the inspection and maintenance of the overhead electric equipment (OHE) on electrified sections.

q: The Anti-Collision Device network named 'Raksha Kavach', designed to prevent train collisions, was developed by:
e: The Anti-Collision Device network Raksha Kavach, fitted on trains to prevent collisions, was developed by the Konkan Railway Corporation.

q: 'BOBRN' wagons of Indian Railways are bottom-discharge hopper wagons mainly used for carrying:
e: BOBRN wagons are bottom-discharge hopper wagons used mainly for carrying bulk commodities like coal and iron ore.

q: 'NMG' wagons of Indian Railways, converted from old passenger coaches, are used mainly for the carriage of:
e: NMG wagons, converted from old passenger coaches, are used mainly for the carriage of automobiles such as cars and two-wheelers.

q: A 'Circular Journey Ticket' issued by Indian Railways allows a passenger to:

options.A: Travel over a circuitous route touching several places and return to the starting station on a single ticket
options.B: Travel free of charge on all suburban trains
options.C: Book tickets only at the station booking office
options.D: Change the class of travel without paying any difference

e: A Circular Journey Ticket allows a passenger to travel over a circuitous route touching several places and return to the starting station on a single ticket.

q: 'Axle counters' provided in railway signalling installations are used to:

options.A: Count the number of passengers in a coach
options.C: Measure the speed of a passing train
options.D: Detect the presence of a train and prove that a section is clear by counting the axles entering and leaving it

e: Axle counters detect the presence of a train by counting the axles entering and leaving a section; when the two counts tally, the section is proved clear.

q: In the year 2022, Indian Railways redesignated the 'Guard' of a train, who is in charge of the train, with the new designation of:
e: In 2022, Indian Railways redesignated the Guard of a train, who is in charge of the train, as Train Manager.

q: The 'Merry-Go-Round' (MGR) system of rail movement is mainly used for:

options.A: Running tourist trains in a circular route
options.B: Dedicated shuttle movement of coal between mines and thermal power plants
options.C: Movement of containers between ports and inland depots
options.D: Movement of parcel vans between metropolitan cities

e: The Merry-Go-Round (MGR) system is a dedicated shuttle arrangement for moving coal between mines and thermal power plants in a continuous cycle.

q: The 25 kV AC system of railway electrification, now standard on Indian Railways, was first introduced in India in 1960 on a section of the:
e: The 25 kV AC system of electrification was first introduced in India in 1960 on a section of the South Eastern Railway and later became the standard system.

q: In terms of total route length, the largest railway network in the world belongs to:
e: The United States of America has the largest railway network in the world in terms of total route length, followed by China and Russia.

q:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Seikan Tunnel of Japan, one of the longest undersea rail tunnels in the world, connects the islands of Honshu and Hokkaido.
2. The Seikan Tunnel carries both rail traffic and road traffic through separate tubes.
Which of the statements is/are correct?
e: Statement 1 is correct: the Seikan Tunnel of Japan connects the islands of Honshu and Hokkaido. Statement 2 is wrong, as the tunnel carries only rail traffic, not road traffic.

q: Attari railway station in Punjab is known as:

options.A: The highest railway station of Punjab
options.B: The last station in India on the rail route towards Lahore in Pakistan
options.C: The largest goods-handling station of Northern Railway
options.D: The first fully solar-powered station of India

e: Attari railway station in Punjab is the last station in India on the rail route towards Lahore in Pakistan.

q: The Allahabad Junction railway station of Uttar Pradesh has been renamed as:
e: Allahabad Junction railway station was renamed Prayagraj Junction, in line with the renaming of the city of Allahabad as Prayagraj.

q: The first stretch of the Kolkata Metro, opened for public service in 1984, ran between:
e: The first stretch of the Kolkata Metro, India's first metro railway opened in 1984, ran between Esplanade and Bhowanipore.

q: The diesel locomotive factory set up in India as a joint venture with General Electric (now Wabtec) is located at Marhowra in the State of:
e: The diesel locomotive factory set up as a joint venture with General Electric (now Wabtec) is located at Marhowra in the Saran district of Bihar.

q: 'President's Rule' in a State of India is imposed by the President under which Article of the Constitution?
e: President's Rule in a State is imposed by the President under Article 356 of the Constitution when the constitutional machinery in the State fails.

q: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House which is not subject to dissolution. One-third of its members retire after every:
e: The Rajya Sabha is a permanent House; its members have six-year terms and one-third of them retire after every two years.

q: Who was the first woman to become the Governor of an Indian State?
e: Sarojini Naidu became the Governor of Uttar Pradesh in 1947 and was the first woman to become the Governor of an Indian State.

q: Under the Constitution of India, the power to form a new State, or to alter the area, boundaries or name of an existing State, is vested in:
e: Under Article 3 of the Constitution, the power to form a new State or alter the area, boundaries or name of an existing State is vested in Parliament.

q: Who was the first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha?
e: Meira Kumar, elected in 2009, was the first woman Speaker of the Lok Sabha.
